# How Can I Track Payments Owed by Buyers After Delivery?


You track payments by linking each delivery to an amount and a due date, updating the status when the payment is received, and using a dashboard to show what is expected, what has arrived, and what is overdue. On **Jestor** , this runs through delivery and receivables **tables** with status fields and dashboard indicators.


Farm sales often involve long payment terms. Without a clear record, it is easy to lose track of what each buyer owes, and late payments are discovered only when cash is already tight.


## What untracked receivables cost


- Overdue payments noticed late
- Cash flow surprises during costly stages of the season
- Disputes about delivered volumes and prices
- No view of which buyers pay on time
- Time spent searching for delivery records when chasing payment


## How receivables tracking works


- Each delivery has a **value** and due date
- Status moves from pending to received or overdue
- A dashboard shows expected receipts by week and month
- Buyer history shows who pays on time and who does not


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Overdue balances are acted on earlier
- Cash flow planning uses real expected receipts
- Buyer reliability becomes visible
- This scales from a few buyers to many


Receivables remembered informally Receivables tracked per delivery


Late discovery of overdue payments Due dates and balances visible


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Does Jestor collect the money?** No, collection is handled through your bank or ERP; Jestor tracks the status. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can the status update from my ERP?** Yes, through the native Omie or Conta Azul integration.


**Can I send a reminder to a buyer?** Yes, automation can send it through email or WhatsApp.
